title: Starting and closing the app
body:
1. Double-click VU3INI Transcribe Studio on the Desktop or in the Start Menu. No terminal window appears.
  2. The app starts its local engine, puts a VU3INI icon in the system tray (near the clock) and opens in your default browser at an address like http://127.0.0.1:PORT.
  3. Read the Terms of Use in the start-up window. The Agree / OK button becomes active after 3 seconds; click it to continue, or click Exit to close the app completely.
  4. If you launch the app again while it is running, it simply brings the existing app back into view.
  5. To close: click Shut down in the top bar, or right-click the tray icon and choose Stop / Exit. Every background process stops; nothing is left running.
  6. Tray icon → Open reopens the app in your browser if you closed the tab.

title: Model packs: what to install first
body:
The speech, speaker and translation models are model packs. Get them once from the Model packs tab (internet needed for that step only), or install .vtpack files you already have.

  • Whisper large-v3-turbo (about 1.6 GB) — the main multilingual engine and language detector. Install this first.
  • IndicWhisper Hindi / Bengali — AI4Bharat models tuned for one language each. When installed, the app automatically uses them for that language.
  • Speaker diarization (about 40 MB) — needed for "Identify speakers".
  • IndicTrans2 en→indic and indic→en — needed for translation.
  • NVIDIA GPU runtime (about 1.9 GB) — lets the app use your NVIDIA graphics card for much faster transcription.

Assamese is transcribed by Whisper large-v3, because AI4Bharat has not published an IndicWhisper checkpoint for Assamese.

title: Getting model packs inside the app
body:
This is the only part of the app that uses the internet, and only when you click the button.

  1. Open the Model packs tab. The Get model packs list shows every available pack with its size; installed ones are marked Installed.
  2. Tick the packs you want (for example Whisper large-v3-turbo, Speaker diarization and the two IndicTrans2 packs).
  3. For a community model, open Add a custom Hugging Face speech model, enter its id (for example anuragshas/whisper-large-v2-as for Assamese), keep the model type Whisper model — convert for speed, and choose its language.
  4. Gated models (the IndicTrans2 packs) need a Hugging Face access token: open the model's page on huggingface.co, accept its terms, create a token under Settings → Access Tokens and paste it into the token box. The token is used for this download only and is never saved.
  5. Tick Also keep the .vtpack files if you want copies to install on another PC.
  6. Click Download and install. Progress (downloaded MB, converting, installing) shows in the queue on the Transcribe tab; you can keep working or cancel. Each pack is installed as soon as it is ready.

title: Installing and removing packs
body:
1. Click the Model packs tab.
  2. Click Install pack from file… and choose a .vtpack file, or paste the file's full path (for example D:\packs\whisper-large-v3-turbo.vtpack) and click Install from path. Installing from a path is faster for big packs because the file is not copied through the browser.
  3. Progress shows in the queue on the Transcribe tab. When it finishes, the pack appears in the table.
  4. To remove a pack, click Remove on its row. You can reinstall it later from the same file.

title: Choosing the engine for each language
body:
1. Open the Model packs tab and scroll to Engine for each language.
  2. Each language (Assamese, Hindi, Bengali, English…) has a dropdown. Packs that support the language are listed first under "Supports …"; any other installed speech pack is listed under "Other packs".
  3. Automatic (the default) shows in brackets which pack it would use: a language-specific pack such as IndicWhisper Hindi when installed, otherwise the multilingual Whisper pack.
  4. Pick a pack for any language you want to fix, then click Save choices. Reset all to Automatic clears every choice.
  5. Your choice is used whenever the Engine is set to Automatic — for files, folders, Live mode and "Transcribe again". The queue shows a note such as "Using IndicWhisper Hindi for Hindi (your choice in Model packs)".
  6. With the language set to Automatic, the language is detected first and then the pack chosen for that language is used.
  7. If you remove a chosen pack, that language goes back to Automatic and the dropdown says so.

title: Transcribing a file
body:
1. Open the Transcribe tab.
  2. Choose the Language (Automatic, Assamese, Hindi, Bengali, English…) and the Engine (Automatic routes each language to the best installed pack).
  3. Optional: tick Identify speakers (and set the number of speakers if you know it; 0 = automatic), Reduce noise, Normalise loudness or Trim long silences.
  4. Drag audio or video files onto the box, or click it to choose files. Several files can be added at once.
  5. Each file joins the Queue with a progress bar and an estimate of the time left.
  6. When a job finishes, click Open to edit the transcript. It is also listed under Recent projects.

title: Languages, engines and mixed-language speech
body:
• Automatic language: the first 30 seconds are checked by Whisper's language detector, then the job is routed to the best pack for that language.
  • Engine = Automatic: a language-specific pack (such as IndicWhisper Hindi) is preferred when installed; otherwise the multilingual Whisper pack is used.
  • Mixed-language speech (Settings): when the language is Automatic, each segment's language is detected separately, which helps with Assamese/Hindi/English mixed in one conversation.
  • Choose a fixed language when you know it — it is faster and avoids wrong detections on short clips.

title: Transcribing a whole folder
body:
1. On the Transcribe tab, open Transcribe a whole folder.
  2. Paste the folder path, for example D:\Recordings\Interviews. Tick Include sub-folders if needed.
  3. Set the language and options above as usual, then click Add folder to queue.
  4. Every audio/video file is copied into the app and transcribed one after another. Your original files are never changed.

title: The queue: pause, resume and cancel
body:
• Jobs run one at a time so they never fight over the graphics card.
  • Pause queue stops new jobs from starting (the running job finishes). Resume queue continues.
  • Cancel stops a queued or running job.
  • Clear finished removes finished, failed and cancelled jobs from the list.
  • If the GPU runs out of memory, the job automatically continues on the CPU and the queue shows a note.

title: Editing a transcript
body:
1. Open a project from the queue, Recent projects or the Projects tab.
  2. Click any word to play the audio from that word. Click the time at the left of a line to play from the start of that segment.
  3. Click into the text to correct it. Word timings are kept for unchanged lines and spread evenly over edited lines.
  4. Hover a line to show its tools: ✂ Split at the cursor (or press Ctrl+Enter), ⤓ Merge with the next line, 🗑 Delete.
  5. Rename the project in the title box and add Tags (comma-separated) to organise projects.
  6. Click Save (or press Ctrl+S). "● unsaved" shows when you have changes.
  7. History ▾ lists earlier saved versions. Choose one to restore it; the current text is kept as another version.

title: Player and waveform
body:
• Use ▶ Play, ⏪ 5s and 5s ⏩, or the keyboard shortcuts.
  • Speed changes playback speed from 0.5× to 2× for careful proofreading.
  • Click the waveform to jump to that point and select the segment there.
  • Fix segment timing: select a segment, then drag the dark handles at its start or end on the waveform.
  • Zoom enlarges the waveform; scroll the mouse wheel over it to move through the audio. Follow keeps the playing line and the current text in view.

title: Speakers (diarization)
body:
1. Install the Speaker diarization pack.
  2. Tick Identify speakers before transcribing, or in the editor click Find speakers again on an existing project.
  3. Speakers appear as "Speaker 1", "Speaker 2"… In the Speakers panel, type real names; they change everywhere at once.
  4. Change who is speaking on any line with the speaker chip at the left of the text. + Add speaker creates a new name.
  5. Talk time shows how long and how many turns each person spoke.

title: Find and replace, custom vocabulary and corrections
body:
• In the editor, type in Find… to highlight every match; type a replacement and click Replace all.
  • Custom vocabulary (Settings): list names, places, call signs or technical terms, one per line. They are given to the model as hints so they are recognised and spelled correctly.
  • Automatic corrections (Settings): one rule per line as wrong => right. They are applied to every new transcript.

title: Confidence heatmap
body: Tick Confidence heatmap in the editor. Words the model was unsure about are shaded: red (very unsure), orange, then yellow. Hover a word to see its confidence and time. Check shaded words first when proofreading.

title: Roman script view
body: Set Show to Roman script to see Assamese, Bengali or Hindi text transliterated into Latin letters (ITRANS style), useful for readers who do not read the native script. This view is read-only; switch back to Original to edit.

title: Translation (IndicTrans2)
body:
1. Install the IndicTrans2 pack for the direction you need: en→indic (English to Assamese/Hindi/Bengali…), indic→en, or indic→indic.
  2. Open a project, choose the target language in the Translate panel and click Translate.
  3. When it finishes, set Show to Translation or Original + translation.
  4. Exports can contain the original, the translation, or both (Export ▾ → Text).
  5. If you edit, split or merge lines afterwards, translate again to keep the translation in step.

title: Exporting
body:
1. In the editor, click Export ▾.
  2. Choose what text to export (Original, Translation or Both) and whether to include speaker names and timestamps.
  3. Pick a format:
    • SRT / WebVTT — subtitles for video players and YouTube.
    • TXT — plain text. DOCX — Word, with a colour per speaker. PDF — with Assamese/Bengali/Hindi fonts embedded so it prints correctly anywhere.
    • JSON — full data including word timings. CSV — opens in Excel.
    • Shareable HTML page — one file with the audio built in; anyone can click a line to hear it.
    • Video with burned-in subtitles — only for video projects; the subtitled MP4 downloads when ready.

Files go to your browser's Downloads folder.

title: Live microphone transcription
body:
1. Open the Live tab. Choose the language (Automatic works too) and engine, and optionally a name.
  2. Click ● Start and allow microphone access in the browser when asked.
  3. Speak normally. Grey italic text is a quick preview; each finished sentence appears in the list with its time.
  4. Click ■ Stop. The recording and transcript are saved as a project; click Open in editor to correct and export it.

A GPU makes live mode much more responsive. On CPU, use a smaller Whisper pack for live work.

title: Projects and search
body:
• The Projects tab lists every transcript with its length, language and tags.
  • The search box looks through project names, tags and the text of every transcript. Click a result to open it at that moment in the audio.
  • Click ✕ on a project card to delete the project and its audio permanently.

title: Settings
body:
• Processor: Automatic uses the NVIDIA GPU when the GPU runtime pack is installed, otherwise the CPU.
  • Precision: float16 for GPUs; int8+float16 uses less GPU memory; int8 is the fast CPU choice.
  • Beam size: higher is slightly more accurate but slower (5 is a good default).
  • Skip silence: voice activity detection removes silent parts before transcribing.
  • Hallucination guard: removes invented lines such as "Thank you for watching" and endless repeats in silent or noisy passages.
  • Default language/engine and the default processing options pre-fill the Transcribe and Live tabs.
  • Click Save settings. The folder where projects and packs are stored is shown at the bottom.

title: Using your NVIDIA graphics card
body:
1. Get the NVIDIA GPU runtime pack on the Model packs tab and keep your NVIDIA driver up to date.
  2. In Settings, set Processor to Automatic or NVIDIA GPU, and Precision to Automatic.
  3. The Model packs tab shows which processor is in use.
  4. With 8 GB of GPU memory, Whisper large-v3-turbo runs comfortably in float16. If memory runs short, choose int8+float16; jobs also fall back to CPU automatically.

title: Dark and light theme
body: Click the round half-filled button in the top bar to switch between dark and light. Your choice is remembered.

title: Keyboard shortcuts
body:
• Ctrl+Space play/pause · Alt+←/→ back/forward 5 s
  • Alt+↑/↓ previous/next segment · Alt+[/] slower/faster
  • Ctrl+S save · Ctrl+Enter split at cursor · F1 this guide · Esc close dialogs

title: Offline use and privacy
body:
• Everything runs on this PC. Audio, transcripts and models never leave it.
  • The app blocks its own outbound internet connections and has no telemetry, update checks or sign-in. The only exception is Download and install on the Model packs tab, which contacts Hugging Face, GitHub, PyPI and AI4Bharat to fetch the packs you ticked.
  • The web page is served only to this PC (address 127.0.0.1) and cannot be opened from other computers.
  • Projects are stored in %LOCALAPPDATA%\VU3INI Transcribe Studio.

title: Troubleshooting
body:
• "No speech recognition model is installed" — get the Whisper large-v3-turbo pack on the Model packs tab.
  • A pack download fails with "No internet connection" — check the connection and try again; for "gated" errors, paste a Hugging Face token.
  • Transcription is slow — install the NVIDIA GPU runtime pack, or use int8 precision on CPU; close other heavy programs.
  • GPU not detected — update the NVIDIA driver, make sure the GPU runtime pack is installed, then restart the app.
  • Wrong language detected — choose the language yourself instead of Automatic.
  • Repeated or invented lines — keep Hallucination guard and Skip silence on.
  • The browser tab was closed — use the tray icon → Open.
  • Logs are in %LOCALAPPDATA%\VU3INI Transcribe Studio\logs.

title: About
body: Help → About shows the version, the author (Sasanka Boruah -VU3INI, hamvu3ini@gmail.com), the open-source projects this app builds on, and every bundled component with its licence.
